To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SNMP traffic is highly asymmetric, with the majority of traffic being generated from the management station, and that the majority of the traffic is caused by polling.
SNMP is a protocol that can be used to manage networks effectively, but that it does suffer from the performance problems associated with a client-server architecture.

(1) the network management system has a very low impact on the overall network traffic, (2) the network management platform has very little impact on the overall system throughput, (3) the system has a very small impact on the overall response time of the network, (4) the system has very little impact upon the overall system reliability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an agent-based approach to network management and the evaluation of the performance of the resulting system through the use of simulation.
the development of a new network management architecture which is based on a distributed agent paradigm.
the behaviour of SNMP and its effect on network traffic and the performance of the network management platform itself.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the behaviour of SNMP, and of the network management system as a whole, is very sensitive to the network environment in which it is operating.
the behaviour of the network management platform is not a significant factor in the behaviour of the system as a whole.
the use of SNMPv1 is not recommended for the monitoring of large networks, and that it is particularly unsuitable for use with wide area links.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while SNMPv1 is not a particularly efficient system, its performance is not so poor that the use of a client-server paradigm is necessarily a bad idea.
the use of SNMPv1 is not a good choice for a network management system, and that SNMPv2c is not an improvement on SNMPv1.

the use of SNMP in a network management platform does not have the detrimental effects on the performance of the system that have been predicted in the literature, and that the performance of the platform can be maintained even when a significant number of network faults are being monitored.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in general, the network management platform does not suffer from performance degradation due to SNMP traffic, but that there may be a problem when the management platform has to deal with a number of faults occurring at the same time.

the behaviour of a system which is used to collect information from a network in response to faults is significantly different from that of a system which simply monitors a properly functioning network.
the use of SNMP in the manner we have simulated does not result in a significant increase in the traffic on the network.
